subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — Skyline Therapeutics commit mismatch and sloting request
messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha@skyline-thera.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Erik Lund <erik.lund@procurement.cobalt-sys.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity — upcoming Q2 ramp (commit mismatch)

Ben —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We signed the committed capacity term sheet for a 12-month Dedicated package (Q2 start) and our legal/finance team just spotted a mismatch between the committed GPU-hours in the DocuSign attachment and the execution plan your operations team has provisioned.

Short version: the commit in DocuSign is for 2x rtx-a40-equivalent reserved pools with a 1.5x burst lane. The provisioning ticket shows a single 2-GPU pool shared with other deals, not isolated. Our launch timeline for the model evaluation (internal POC → pilot → prod) is tight: heavy inference traffic starts the week of April 19.

We need two things urgently:
- Confirmation of isolation (dedicated vs shared) and expected throughput/latency for our traffic profile (typical seq=1024, mix of chat + batch scoring).
- If you cannot deliver isolated pools by April 19, what are the contingency options — burst guarantees, prioritized tranche, or credits/refund?

I’ve attached the signed commit summary. Can you loop in the capacity team and confirm today if possible? Our VP will escalate otherwise.

—Asha
Skyline Therapeutics
Ops Lead

Thanks for the flag and for attaching the DocuSign summary. I’m sorry for the confusion — that’s definitely not the experience we want to give you heading into the ramp. I’m looping in Karthik (infrastructure) and Monica (your CSM/sales) to triage.

Immediate plan:
- Karthik, can you confirm the current provisioning snapshot for DL-2027-1374 and whether the pools were created as dedicated isolates or as soft-shared capacity?
- Monica, can you surface any negotiated SLA that explicitly calls isolation? I’ll put a hold on ticket changes until we get confirmation.

Asha — I’ll set a hard follow-up for EOD Pacific and include options if we cannot meet April 19. We’ll treat this as an escalation.

Ben

Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — upcoming Q2 ramp (commit mismatch)

Ben / Monica —

Investigated provisioning state: the ticket we raised on Apr 1 created a 2-GPU pool in the shared-tranche namespace ("dedicated-ish") because the SRE onboarding flow used the default allocation template. That template reserves 2x A40-equivalent slots but places them as affinity-isolated within a multi-tenant node group (workload isolation via cgroups/KV cache namespace, not physically separate node reservation).

Implications for Skyline: at the expected seq=1024 chat profile, shared-tranche gives you the logical isolation we typically offer, but it does not meet the contractual language for "physically dedicated pools". The engineering difference is: preemption risk is near-zero but noisy neighbor tail-latency can appear under cluster pressure; your prefix/KV cache is still tenant-scoped.

Options (tradeoffs + ETA):
1) Convert to physically isolated pool (true Dedicated) — requires reserving two full nodes; ETA 7 business days (ETA: Apr 12–14, but this assumes no upstream capacity commits).
2) Keep shared-tranche but add high-priority ingress routing + guaranteed burst lane (soft SLO) — ETA 48–72 hours; lower cost and faster.
3) Short-term: shift some heavy batch scoring to a scheduled off-peak window (we can set dedicated batch workers on cheaper instances) — ETA 24 hours to setup schedule.

If Skyline requires a guaranteed physically isolated pool by Apr 19, we need authorization to either: 1) preempt some reserved capacity (would require commercial tradeoffs with other deals), or 2) use uncommitted spot of equivalent hardware (best-effort) until true nodes are available. I recommend we surface both the commercial and operational tradeoffs to the customer.

I’ve attached a quick tranche-swap matrix to illustrate options.

Karthik
Sr. Infra Engineer — Serving Runtime

Attachment: proposed_tranche_swap_matrix.xlsx (stub)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Asha Rao <asha@skyline-thera.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — upcoming Q2 ramp (commit mismatch)

Asha / team —

Thanks for bringing this up, Asha. Apologies for the paperwork/provisioning mismatch — that’s on us. Contractually, the DocuSign does include language for "physically isolated dedicated pools" in section 2.b. However: we are entering a period of tight fleet utilization across our US region and several Q2 deals are overlapping.

Commercial options I’m prepared to offer immediately (subject to leadership and finance):
- Option A (Rapid convert): We convert Skyline to a physically isolated 2-node pool. We can do this by adjusting current commit tranches, but that would require either a swap with a lower-priority reserved customer (we’d offer them a temporary burst lane + credit) or a short-term mobilization of burst hardware. Cost impact: incremental one-time conversion fee + monthly uplift reflected in amended SOW.
- Option B (Priority burst + SLA credit): Keep the current logical isolation, attach a guaranteed high-priority routing policy and offer a 10% monthly credit if we see any P95 latency breaches for production windows. Faster, lower cost.
- Option C (Phased delivery): Dedicated pool delivered on Apr 13; in the meantime we apply Option B.

Ask: Ben / Karthik / Priyom, please confirm operational feasibility (ETA & exact wording for SLA credit) so I can share a clear proposal with Asha by EOD. Asha — if you can confirm which option you prefer we’ll draft an amendment and get DocuSign moved quickly.

Monica Patel
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Asha Rao <asha@skyline-thera.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — upcoming Q2 ramp (commit mismatch) — allocation decision and next steps

Team / Asha —

Operational decision and next steps: after reviewing tranche availability and the active slate of Q2 conversions, we can commit to Option C (Phased delivery):
- Short-term (by Apr 7): apply high-priority ingress routing + dedicate a guaranteed burst lane for Skyline during their production windows (we will codify P95 targets and a 10% credit clause as proposed). This is a configuration change only — no node reservation — ETA 48 hours.
- Medium-term (by Apr 14): convert the Skyline allocation to a physically isolated 2-node pool (physical reservation). To do this we will reassign one node from an underutilized committed deal (Deal ID: DL-2026-0980). That customer has agreed to a temporary burst-credit in exchange for a tranche swap (commercials to be handled by Monica).

Operational caveats:
- The reassign will show as a reserve re-schedule in our capacity ledger for Apr 14 and will cause a short-lived leaderboard reshuffle; we expect no customer-impact if routing is configured correctly.
- Priyom / finance: please pre-authorize the conversion fee workflow so Monica can finalize the SOW amendment without delay.

Asha — I will schedule a 30-min handoff call tomorrow (Apr 6) with you, Karthik and Monica to confirm production windows and runbook items (cache priming, kv namespace warming, and routing policies). If you’d prefer we can accelerate to Apr 12 but it requires a second tranche swap.

I’ll follow up with the new SOW language for the credit SLA and a timeline.

Sean Gallagher
Capacity & Fleet Operations
Redwood Inference
